script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for November 28. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
You live somewhere.  But are you just located there, or are you part of it?  Citizenship is more than address—it's belonging.

You're a citizen of multiple communities simultaneously: neighborhood, city, nation, world. Each level has its own participation opportunities. Engagement at any level matters. Citizenship bundles rights (vote, access services) with duties (pay taxes, serve if called).  Good citizenship means claiming both sides—receiving benefits and meeting obligations.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: You're not just in a community; you're part of it.  Belonging includes both receiving and giving.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Citizenship Check - How Do You Participate?.

Here's your activity: How do you currently participate in your communities—neighborhood, city, nation? What could you do more? Choose one way to be a more active citizen this week—attend a meeting, help a neighbor, learn about local issues. This helps you assess and expand civic participation.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about being part of a place can be applied to citizenship check - how do you participate?. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
